headline: Highest risk is medium: Gemini CLI can write/egress into shared files and MCP, while python-cheatsheet is read-only documentation with no execution surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files, use MCP, and parse stdin/stdout, so malicious content in shared files or MCP outputs could steer it. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot actively inject, but if Gemini consumes its content as instructions, the pathway exists. No shared channel is documented beyond files/git.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI is pointed at a workspace containing attacker-controlled markdown or prompts
IF Gemini CLI is configured to trust MCP/file content as instructions
mitigations: Review and sanitize shared files before Gemini reads them
Disable or restrict MCP servers for the session
Use a separate workspace for untrusted content
Require explicit confirmation before executing file-derived instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI can read files and has broad network egress, so it could leak local workspace content if given sensitive files. python-cheatsheet has no filesystem read, no network, and no data classes touched, so it is not a leakage source. The pair lacks a shared writable workspace in B, keeping blast radius limited.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Gemini CLI's working directory
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to transmit retrieved file contents to external APIs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Run Gemini CLI in a dedicated directory
Block network egress for sensitive sessions

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; python-cheatsheet cannot write, modify git, or spawn processes. That makes direct write-write conflict impossible, and the only overlap is read-only content. No locking issue is evident because B has no mutable surface.
conditions: IF python-cheatsheet is replaced with a writable agent in the same repo
IF Gemini CLI is run concurrently with another writer on the same git checkout
mitigations: Avoid concurrent writers in the same checkout
Enable git locks or serialized commits

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code or text that a downstream consumer might trust, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not act on outputs. Without an action-taking B, the cascade stops at content generation, so the blast radius is limited to misleading documentation or prompts.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI output is copied into a downstream workflow that treats it as authoritative
IF a separate agent is added after python-cheatsheet to execute the content
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of Gemini output
Keep documentation and execution steps separate
Add verification checks before any downstream action

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evident from the profiles: Gemini CLI handles local code/files and optional Google login, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no regulated data classes. There is no documented PHI, EU PII, residency, or retention conflict to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later used on regulated data classes not listed in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Document any future residency or retention requirements
Review data handling before enabling new workflows
